LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION – PARAGRAPHS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Writing for information – Paragraphs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.1 Writing for information – Paragraphs, part of Strand 3 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write paragraphs? 2. Why is it important to preserve wildlife?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm with peers the features of a well-developed paragraph,

2. work with peers to study a collection of paragraphs,

3. collaborate with peers to review the paragraphs and identify whether they are well developed and written,

4. prepare a sketch of ideas related to the theme,

5. use the sketched ideas to compose a paragraph on the theme,

6. share their paragraphs with peers for review,

7. display the best written paragraphs in the class gallery,

8. conduct a writing contest to identify well developed paragraphs from the class. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm with peers the features of a well-developed paragraph,
2. work with peers to study a collection of paragraphs,
3. collaborate with peers to review the paragraphs and identify whether they are well developed and written,
4. prepare a sketch of ideas related to the theme,
5. use the sketched ideas to compose a paragraph on the theme,
6. share their paragraphs with peers for review,
7. display the best written paragraphs in the class gallery,
8. conduct a writing contest to identify well developed paragraphs from the class. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Writing for information – Paragraphs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks engagingly when brainstorming with peers the features of a well- developed paragraph.

• Creativity and Imagination. This is developed as the learner shares creative ideas when conducting a writing contest to

identify well developed paragraphs from the class.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with others to share their paragraphs with peers for review.

• Integrity: The learner shows transparency by displaying the best written paragraphs in the class gallery.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education. This is promoted as the learner prepares a paragraph sketch on a topic related to the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of paragraph writing to their learning in English.
